gloss: to run through; to dash through

definitions.gloss: to run through; to dash through
definitions.explanation: To run quickly through a place from one end to the other without stopping.
To pass through a period of time quickly, often used figuratively for busy or intense times.

examples.japanese: {風|かぜ}が{野原|のはら}を{駆|か}け{抜|ぬ}ける。
examples.english: The wind rushes through the field.

examples.japanese: {選手|せんしゅ}がゴールまで{一気|いっき}に{駆|か}け{抜|ぬ}けた。
examples.english: The athlete raced straight through to the goal.

examples.japanese: {青春|せいしゅん}を{駆|か}け{抜|ぬ}けた{日々|ひび}。
examples.english: The days that raced through our youth.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しい{一年|いちねん}を{駆|か}け{抜|ぬ}けた。
examples.english: I raced through a busy year.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{短|みじか}い{人生|じんせい}を{全力|ぜんりょく}で{駆|か}け{抜|ぬ}けた{人|ひと}だった。
examples.english: He was someone who lived his short life to the fullest.

notes:
COMPOUND VERB:
{駆|か}ける (to run, to gallop) + {抜|ぬ}ける (to pass through)

TRANSITIVITY:
{自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive) - takes を for the place being passed through

FIGURATIVE USE:
Often used poetically to describe wind, light, or time passing quickly through something.

RELATED COMPOUND VERBS:
- {走|はし}り{抜|ぬ}ける: to run through (similar meaning)
- {駆|か}け{回|まわ}る: to run around
- {突|つ}き{抜|ぬ}ける: to pierce through
